identity.title: Continuum and molecular emission from the inner regions of the symbiotic system R Aquarii

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present very sensitive ALMA maps of the continuum emission at 1.3, 0.9, and 0.45 mm.

evidence.quote: In this work, we assumed a distance of 265$\pm$20 pc for our calculations, which is derived from the luminosity-period relation (cite: alcolea23).
The ICRS coordinates for the maps at 0.9 mm are R.A.: 23:43:49.4962, Dec.: –15:17:04.720.

question.value: What do ALMA continuum, H30alpha and molecular line maps reveal about the inner regions of the symbiotic system R Aqr, and how are weak molecules distributed there?

evidence.quote: Our aim is to study the inner regions of R Aqr based on ALMA observations of the continuum and line emission.

bands.value: Band 6 (1.3 mm), Band 7 (0.9 mm), Band 9 (0.45 mm)

evidence.quote: We explored the emission of this object in the ALMA Bands 6, 7, and  9, corresponding to 1.3, 0.9, and 0.45 mm wavelengths

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 0.282 MHz/channel at 1.3 and 0.9 mm (0.38 and 0.25 km/s), 0.564 MHz/channel at 0.45 mm; spectral windows 25, 27, 29, 31 per band

evidence.quote: we reached a spectral resolution of 0.282 MHz per channel at 1.3 and 0.9 mm  and 0.564 MHz per channel at 0.45 mm

configurations.value: Band 6 C43-6 (low res) and C43-10 (high res); Band 7 C43-8; Band 9 C43-7

angular_resolution.value: 20-250 mas depending on band, configuration and weighting

evidence.quote: Angular resolutions between 20 and 250 mas were attained depending on the observed frequency, array configuration, and mapping weighting.

sensitivity.value: noise ~0.1, 2, 10 mJy in Bands 6, 7, 9 clean maps

evidence.quote: Noise levels of $\sim$0.1, 2, and 10 mJy were found in the clean maps on Bands 6, 7, and 9, respectively.

observing_dates.value: Band 6 June and September 2019; Band 7 November 2017; Band 9 August 2019

evidence.quote: The observations of Band 6 were carried out in June and September 2019 with high- and low-spatial resolution, and Bands 7 and 9 were observed in November 2017 and August 2019, respectively.

what.value: Orbital parameters (period 42.4 yr, PA 95 deg, semi-major axis 57±8 mas) and predicted WD position

evidence.quote: The derived orbital period is 42.4 yr, which is slightly shorter than previous estimations (cite: gromadzki09).

what.value: Photosphere extent and temperature used in model

evidence.quote: has the extent and temperature described in (cite: bujarrabal18)
we assumed a relative abundance of 6.6$\cdot10^{-6}$, which is compatible with the values found in O-rich Mira-type variables (cite: massalkhi20)
The calibration of the visibilities was performed using the standard ALMA pipeline in the CASA software.

flux_calibrator.value: J0006-0623; ~1.45 Jy (Jun 2019) and ~1.32 Jy (Sep 2019) Band 6; ~0.9 Jy Band 7; ~4.3 Jy Band 9

evidence.quote: For the absolute flux scaling, J0006-0623 was used as a calibrator.
Flux uncertainties in Bands 6 and 7 are estimated to be between about 5% and 8%, while it is $\sim$15 % for Band 9.

self_calibration.value: Continuum self-calibration in GILDAS; Band 6 SPW 31 self-calibrated on SiO v=1 J=5-4 maser

evidence.quote: Self-calibration of the *uv* data using the continuum emission was performed by means of GILDAS.
Map cleaning was performed in GILDAS using the Hogbom algorithm implemented in MAPPING.

deconvolver.value: Hogbom; ~4000 components first pass, 5000 final; stop at sigma_p/2

evidence.quote: Final clean maps were obtained imposing a maximum amplitude of the absolute value of the residual map of $\sigma_{p}$/2

weighting_robust.value: robust weighting (value not given); natural weighting for SPW 27 and 29 in Band 6 and low-res maps

evidence.quote: we worked to reach our best angular resolution using robust weighting.

continuum_subtraction.value: Line-free channels averaged and subtracted in uv data

evidence.quote: The continuum is subtracted from the *uv* data affecting the visibilities directly.

array_combination.value: Band 6 high and low resolution merged

evidence.quote: we merged both the high- and low-resolution Band 6 data to increase the S/N

smoothing.value: 1.6 km/s channels for lines; 4.8 km/s for H30alpha

evidence.quote: we resampled the *uv* tables to obtain a spectral resolution of 4.8 km s$^{-1}$, increasing the S/N.

final_beam.value: about 25x18, 35x25, 33x28 mas (Bands 6,7,9); circular 15 and 20 mas continuum beams; 264x163 mas low-res

evidence.quote: Beam sizes of about 25$\times$18, 35$\times$25, and 33$\times$28 mas and PAs of around 129, 56, and 83 deg were achieved for the ALMA Bands 6, 7, and  9.

what.value: Calibration of 2017.1.00363.S data, and similar for 2018.1.00638.S

evidence.quote: The calibration of the 2017.1.00363.S data has been described in (cite: bujarrabal18), and that of 2018.1.00638.S data was very similar, including in the choice of calibrators.

what.value: 0.9 mm continuum already studied in detail, so not reanalysed

evidence.quote: Because the high- and low-resolution continuum maps at 0.9 mm were already studied by (cite: bujarrabal18) in detail, we focused on the analysis of the observations at 1.3 and 0.45 mm.

what.value: Model code similar to earlier radiative transfer codes

evidence.quote: Our code is similar to those extensively used and described previously to model emission of gas in rotation and expansion in evolved objects (cite: gallardo21; bujarrabal17; bujarrabal21).

unstated_but_needed: Line-free channel ranges per spectral window
Self-calibration solution intervals and reference components
Model code and fitting figure of merit; dust Gaussian parameters

method.value: Fit continuum centroid with uv_fit and recentre all uv tables on it

evidence.quote: The coordinates of these centroids were derived from a preliminary analysis of the *uv* tables of the continuum data using the routine *uv_fit* of the GILDAS packages

assumptions.value: Continuum centroid approximates the Mira position

evidence.quote: which approximately gives the position of the Mira component

validation.value: Centroid differences compared with beam size

evidence.quote: These differences are comparable to the position accuracy and much smaller than the beam size of the low-resolution data

method.value: uv-plane continuum subtraction then Hogbom CLEAN with two-pass stopping criteria

evidence.quote: We completed a first cleaning using a maximum number of clean components of $\sim$4000.

assumptions.value: Continuum constant within each spectral window (spectral index 2, <1% variation)

evidence.quote: assuming a spectral index of  two, differences in the intensity of the continuum emission smaller than 1 % are expected

validation.value: Checked line-free channels for residuals and no overcleaning

evidence.quote: We checked that the final clean maps do not show overcleaned regions.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure continuum fluxes and spectral index

method.value: Compare central compact component intensities at 1.3 and 0.45 mm

evidence.quote: By comparing the intensities measured for the compact central component of the high-resolution continuum maps at 1.3 and 0.45 mm, we estimated a spectral index of 1.88.

analysis_steps.goal: Model compact molecular emission (SiO v=0 J=16-15 example)

method.value: LTE ray-tracing model of expanding oblate shell plus in-falling spherical shell with dust and photosphere continuum, continuum subtracted, convolved with beam

evidence.quote: Our model nebula consists of an oblate ellipsoidal shell in radial expansion for the emission and an in-falling spherical shell for the absorption

key_parameters.value: Power-law density and temperature; constant velocity

evidence.quote: we assumed a constant radial velocity to simplify our calculations.

assumptions.value: LTE; optically thin Gaussian dust; SiO abundance 6.6e-6; distance 265 pc

evidence.quote: We assumed local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) to obtain the coefficients of absorption and emission in each point of the circumstellar shells.

fitting.value: Best fit found by manual variation of parameters

evidence.quote: We found the best-fit model by manually varying the parameters to adjust the synthetic maps to the observations.

validation.value: Qualitative comparison with channel maps of other lines; size uncertainty <20% (expanding), ~50% (in-falling)

evidence.quote: We estimated that the uncertainty in the determination of the sizes of the expanding shell and in-falling component is smaller than 20% and $\sim$50%, respectively.
The calibration of the visibilities was performed using the standard ALMA pipeline in the CASA software.

used_for.value: Self-calibration, centroid fitting, cleaning and imaging

evidence.quote: Map cleaning was performed in GILDAS using the Hogbom algorithm implemented in MAPPING.

results_numeric.quantity: Continuum spectral index of central component (1.3-0.45 mm)

evidence.quote: we estimated a spectral index of 1.88

results_numeric.quantity: Central compact continuum flux at 1.3 and 0.45 mm

evidence.quote: The flux of this central component is 30 and 220 mJy at 1.3 and 0.45 mm, respectively.
This atomic line spans a velocity range between –80.6 and 29.8 km s$^{-1}$

results_numeric.quantity: Expanding shell outer radius (equatorial) and expansion velocity

evidence.quote: we accurately derived velocities of 9 and $-$17 km s$^{-1}$ for the expanding and in-falling components, respectively.

results_numeric.quantity: Position angle of expanding shell projection

evidence.quote: the projection of the expanding shell is inclined at a PA of 105°

findings_qualitative.value: H30alpha is displaced west of the 1.3 mm continuum peak, tracing the jet and WD surroundings

evidence.quote: the emission of H30$\alpha$ is slightly displaced to the west of the continuum emission

claims.hypothesis: Does the high-resolution 1.3 mm continuum trace the innermost jet near the WD?
claims.experiment: Compare 1.3 mm high-res continuum with predicted WD position
claims.result: Emission extends toward predicted WD position
claims.finding: Extension is ionized gas around the WD and jet base; cannot be firmly confirmed

evidence.quote: The coincidence with the predicted WD position confirms the predicted orbital parameters and binary movements

claims.hypothesis: Do weak molecules survive only close to the AGB star?
claims.experiment: Map many lines and model SiO with shell model
claims.finding: Weak species confined to intra-orbital regions

evidence.quote: we find that the expanding shell is $\sim$10$^{14}$ cm in size

claims.hypothesis: What causes the central absorption at positive velocities?
claims.finding: Consistent with in-falling gas but photospheric motion cannot be excluded

evidence.quote: we cannot rule out that the radial movements of the photosphere layers yield this spectral feature

limitations_admitted.value: In-falling component size is not conclusive

evidence.quote: Therefore, the obtained result concerning the size of the in-falling component is not conclusive.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fit is manual with no goodness-of-fit metric
Continuum subtraction affects optically thick line centres

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Several hundred GB raw across three bands
reproducibility.score_reason: Data archival but GILDAS imaging parameters and custom model not specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete and model is custom and manually tuned.
